what_this_is: What every locally-hosted published image IS. This is NOT a rights file: image-rights-records.json governs whether PlotNua may publish someone else's image, and this governs what PlotNua's own published images are. A SUPPLIER_IMAGE row here carries a pointer (rights_ref) to that file and duplicates none of it. Nothing in this file grants any permission.

asset_classes.SUPPLIER_IMAGE: Actual supplier imagery, published under a documented permission or a valid licence. Carries rights_ref pointing at the authorising organisation row in image-rights-records.json.
asset_classes.AI_ILLUSTRATION: Independently generated generic imagery that reproduces no supplier photograph and no distinctive product design. Carries the tool, the date, the prompt, an explicit reference_inputs list and a named human review.

the_third_state.name: NO_IMAGE
the_third_state.note: NO_IMAGE is the state of an image SLOT that has no asset. It is deliberately NOT a class in this register, because a register of assets cannot hold a record for an image that does not exist. It is recorded here so the distinction is explicit: every image slot on a published page resolves to exactly one of three states, two of which point at a record in this file and the third of which points at nothing. NO_IMAGE must stay as easy to choose as the other two -- if it is not a respectable answer, the pressure is always to fill the slot with something, and that pressure is how laundering starts.

rules: Never use AI to launder a copyrighted image.
AI generation is never evidence of rights. No code path reads this file to answer a rights question.
Never imply an AI illustration depicts a named supplier's actual product.
An absent term is never an inclusion: an asset with no record is undeclared, not cleared.
AI illustrations do not appear on individual supplier product cards. product-card is not an available permitted surface.
Provenance is never inferred from appearance.

They are neither a supplier's image nor an AI illustration, so the approved three-state taxonomy has no place for a first-party photograph. how_to_declare_an_asset: 1. Establish what made the image, from real knowledge. If that is not available, do not declare it.
2. Move its entry from legacy_undeclared to records, keeping the asset path and recomputing sha256.

3. For AI_ILLUSTRATION: record tool, date, prompt verbatim, an explicit reference_inputs array (empty is an assertion, absent is an unanswered question), depicts_named_product false, depicts_named_organisation false, a named human_review, and permitted_surfaces.
4. For SUPPLIER_IMAGE: record rights_ref only. Copy no permission data.
6. Only once records exist may the corresponding page captions be labelled.
label_note: An undeclared asset gets NO label. Inventing a classification to fill a caption is the error this register exists to prevent, and no published caption changes until the matching record exists.
legacy_undeclared_note: THE RATCHET. Every asset below is enumerated by path and sha256. The guard refuses any local image on a published page that is in neither records nor this list, so no NEW undeclared image can be added. The count is printed on every CI run and only ever goes down. A legacy entry is NOT a declaration, is NOT verified, is NOT authorised supplier imagery, and may not reach a product card or a supplier context.

records.prompt:
TASK: Transform this reference image into an exceptionally
photorealistic architectural photograph.

This image is intended to become the flagship BEFORE image
for PlotNua, an Irish property discovery platform.

The objective is to make the image indistinguishable from
a genuine photograph of a suburban Irish property.

CRITICAL: THIS IS AN IMAGE-TO-IMAGE REFINEMENT TASK.

Do not redesign the property.
Do not reinterpret the composition.
Do not create a different house.
Do not change the camera angle.

Use the supplied image as the precise visual reference.

THE SCENE

A typical detached two-storey Irish suburban house,
photographed from a slightly elevated position overlooking
its rear garden.

The house has:
- Cream rendered exterior walls.
- Traditional brown roof tiles.
- Chimney and roof window.
- Existing white-framed windows.
- Single-storey rear extension.
- Patio with ordinary garden furniture.
- A large, slightly imperfect lawn.
- Timber garden boundaries.
- A narrow side garden with a mature tree.
- A believable residential street behind the property.
- Neighbouring suburban houses.

PRESERVE ALL OF THESE FEATURES.

PHOTOGRAPHIC REALISM

The final result should look like an actual photograph
taken with a professional full-frame camera and a
high-quality architectural lens.

Natural daylight.
Realistic shadows.
Accurate perspective.
Physically believable materials.
Natural atmospheric depth.
Subtle photographic imperfections.

Avoid the excessively sharp, overly saturated,
artificially perfect appearance associated with
AI-generated architectural images.

SPECIFIC IMPROVEMENTS

1. CARS

The cars currently look slightly AI-generated.

Replace or refine them so that they resemble
completely believable, ordinary cars parked along
an Irish residential street.

Correct proportions, wheels, windows, reflections,
shadows and perspective.

Avoid distorted bodywork or unusual vehicle shapes.

Do not add more cars than necessary.

2. NEIGHBOURING HOUSES

Make the neighbouring houses look like genuine,
individually built suburban Irish homes.

Avoid repetitive architecture, duplicated windows,
impossible rooflines and artificial-looking details.

Maintain the existing residential street layout.

3. STREET

Ensure the road behind the property is geographically
and architecturally coherent.

The road should connect naturally through the
neighbourhood.

Include believable footpaths, kerbs and driveways.

Do not create disconnected roads or impossible junctions.

4. VEGETATION

Make the trees, hedges, shrubs and lawn appear
photographically authentic.

Avoid duplicated foliage patterns, unnaturally
perfect plants and excessively vivid green colours.

The grass should retain natural variations,
slightly patchy areas and ordinary wear.

5. HOUSE DETAILS

Improve the realism of the roof tiles, windows,
gutters, doors, render and patio.

Keep the house deliberately ordinary.

DO NOT modernise or renovate it.

The dramatic renovation will happen in a separate
AFTER image.

6. LIGHTING AND COLOUR

Natural Irish late-spring or summer daylight.

Soft, believable sunlight.
Natural shadows.
Realistic sky.
Balanced exposure.
Authentic photographic colour grading.

Avoid HDR effects, exaggerated contrast,
cinematic orange-and-teal grading and
artificial architectural-render lighting.

STRICT COMPOSITION RULES

Keep exactly the same:

- Camera viewpoint and framing.
- House position and proportions.
- Roof geometry.
- Garden dimensions.
- Left-side garden.
- Mature tree location.
- Main lawn.
- Patio location.
- Garden boundaries.
- Residential street position.
- Neighbouring property positions.

Do not crop or zoom.

Do not add any new garden structures.

No solar panels.
No garden room.
No treehouse.
No sauna.
No greenhouse.
No raised vegetable beds.
No house renovation.

These will be introduced later as part of
PlotNua's interactive transformation experience.

OUTPUT

A single ultra-high-resolution, landscape-format,
photorealistic architectural photograph.

Maintain the original image's aspect ratio.

No text.
No logos.
No watermarks.
No annotations.

SUCCESS CRITERION

A viewer should believe this is an authentic
photograph of a real Irish suburban property,
not an AI-generated image.

The property must remain identical to the reference
so that it can subsequently be used as the master
BEFORE image for an interactive BEFORE/AFTER slider.

- long, low raised beds (about 15 cm high) with weathered steel or old timber edges, running along the strip, with narrow mown grass paths between them, and two shorter beds on the lawn in front of the patio;
- mature vegetables at different stages: lettuces, chard, cavolo nero kale, leeks, beetroot, carrots, parsley and chives. Some plants larger than others, some gaps, a few yellowing or slug-nibbled leaves, dark crumbly soil showing between plants;
- one or two low white mesh tunnels over part of a bed;
- a small, discreet slatted compost bin in weathered silver-grey timber and a slim water butt beside it, at the near end of the strip against the hedge;
- a wooden crate of freshly picked vegetables on a path.

staged_composites_note: STAGED COMPOSITES (H2, 20 Oct 2026). A locked composite whose provenance is recorded before publication. It names no asset, so nothing on a page can be accounted for by it. Checked by P6 and P13. It grants nothing: the permission lives in image-adaptation-licences.json, reached only through rights_ref (organisation_code + atlas_permission_ref), exactly as P4 reaches the rights manifest.
brand_vector_derivatives_note: BRAND VECTOR DERIVATIVES (22 Oct 2026, founder-approved Atlas symbol C). Each entry is a pure vector redrawn from brand artwork this register already holds, bound to each source's exact sha256. It inherits its sources' provenance state (both sources are LEGACY_UNDECLARED, so this is NOT a declaration and NOT verified), carries no class, label or rights field, and is not counted in legacy_undeclared, so the ratchet is unchanged. The guard (P14) refuses one whose source changed, whose source is not brand artwork, that embeds or links any image or external resource, that records no founder approval, or that no page shows.
